equivalent_mutants_not_declared.mutant: if pattern is None: -> if False:
equivalent_mutants_not_declared.why_no_test_can_kill_it: The raise it lets through (NoneType has no attribute 'match') propagates out of permitted() into this module's own fail-safe wrapper, which exits 0 with empty stdout. That is the SAME observable behaviour as the guard: silence, exit 0. The guard is KEPT because leaning on the last-resort wrapper for ordinary control flow means every Bash call on a uid-less machine raises internally - but no external observer can tell, so no case may declare it.

equivalent_mutants_not_declared.mutant: if not line.startswith("/") or FORBIDDEN & set(line): -> if False:
equivalent_mutants_not_declared.why_no_test_can_kill_it: Both halves are defence in depth over a check that already holds downstream. A relative root yields a pattern with no leading slash, and sandboxed() refuses any token that does not start with one before it ever matches. A metacharacter survives re.escape as a literal, so it can only ever match a path spelled with that literal. The guard STAYS: it is what keeps this file correct if sandboxed()'s own leading-slash check is ever relaxed.
